jo: Follow-up from postmortem: recurring long-context bursts caused p99 spikes and temporary throughput loss. Need SLO changes, owners, and dashboard + runbook work.

dean: Short proposal: keep p95 stable, add a temporary p99 guardrail for 14 days, and introduce a throughput SLO for dedicated pools. Draft below.

rachel: I'll take dashboards/alerts. Plan: token-size histogram, per-instance queue depth, kv-cache miss rate, error-budget burn. ETA 6 days.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-453 | Sev2 | start=2185009000 | end=2185010500 | link=https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-453

dean: Draft SLOs (for discussion):
- inference_latency interactive: p95 <= 220ms (30d), p99 <= 1.0s (14d temporary)
- dedicated_throughput: qps_per_gpu >= 110 (7d window)

jo: Action items:
- dean: open SLO PR with rollback criteria + measurement notes (due 2026-04-18)
- rachel: dashboard + alert PR (first pass due 2026-04-20)
- tier2: add token-aware admission-control prototype and perf sim (due 2026-04-19)
- jo: update postmortem tracker and create recurring 2-week "long-context review" until 30d stable

tier2: question: fallback vs soft-throttle? I'd prototype soft-throttle with Retry-After header and sampled fallback for degraded routing.

dean: Agree. Gate any fallback with quality sampling and canary CI checks. Rollback if sampled quality drift >5% or client errors up >1%.

rachel: Alerts: sustained p99 > 950ms for 3m -> page; queue_depth > 150 for 2m -> page; kv_miss > 30% for 5m -> channel. Will attach playbook links.

jo: OK owners acked. We'll sync next Monday for PR reviews. If timelines shift, update here. :thumbsup:
